sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Tripartite Structure**: Unique UN agency bringing together governments, employers, and workers representatives in its executive bodies.
• **Establishment & Nobel Peace Prize**: Created in **1919** by the Treaty of Versailles as an affiliated agency of the League of Nations; became the first specialized agency of the UN in **1946**. Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in **1969**.
• **Headquarters**: Located in **Geneva, Switzerland**.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Adopts international labour standards through **Conventions** (legally binding treaties when ratified) and **Recommendations** (non-binding guidelines).

items.definition: The 'Parliament of Labour' that meets annually in Geneva to set international labour standards and adopt the ILO budget.
The executive council of the ILO that meets three times a year in Geneva, making policy decisions and drafting the agenda for the ILC.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Global Presence**: Operates through regional offices in Africa, Americas, Arab States, Asia and the Pacific, and Europe and Central Asia.
• **Decent Work Technical Support Teams (DWT)**: Decentralized hubs providing technical guidance and policy advisory services directly to member states.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: High rates of global informal employment, rise of platform/gig economies, and uneven ratification of core conventions.
• **Policy Interventions**: India's recent amalgamation of 29 central labour laws into **4 Labour Codes** aligned with principles of ILO conventions on occupational safety, wages, and social security.

items.title: Mnemonic for India's Unratified Core Conventions
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "India CANNOT yet join 87 and 98"
• **Decoded Meaning**: India has NOT ratified ILO Convention **87** (Freedom of Association and Protection of the Right to Organise) and Convention **98** (Right to Organise and Collective Bargaining) due to domestic civil service conduct rules restricting union rights for government employees.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Directly answers statements claiming India has ratified all 8 fundamental conventions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Out of 8 fundamental conventions, India has ratified **6** (Missing: 87 & 98). Out of 4 governance conventions, India has ratified **2** (C81 and C144).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that 'ratification of an ILO convention automatically makes it binding domestic law in India.' This is FALSE. International treaties require explicit domestic legislative enactment in India.
Mains Value Addition: Cite the ILO's 'World Employment and Social Outlook' report or 'Decent Work' framework while structuring answers on unemployment, formalization, and labor reforms.

keyTakeaways: The ILO is the sole tripartite UN agency uniting governments, employers, and workers.
India has ratified 6 out of the 8 fundamental ILO conventions, omitting Conventions 87 and 98.
Labour standards are established via Conventions (binding upon ratification) and Recommendations (non-binding).
